10036318:
Maine Professional Guides Association
www.maineguides.org
Testimony in Opposition to LD 777 An Act to Standardize the Muzzle-loading Season Statewide
March 10, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the committee, my name is James Cote and I am submitting this testimony on behalf of the Maine Professional Guides Association in opposition to LD 777. LD 777 would require that the muzzleloader season on deer must be the same in all areas of the state. While we believe that this legislation is well intended, we are concerned that it may also have unintended consequences. First, we are concerned that in certain years, where we experience significant snow depths in early December, that adding an additional week of muzzleloader seasons to northern wildlife management districts could mean an over-harvest of deer going to yards for the winter. Secondly, we are also concerned that by requiring muzzleloader season to be the same in all areas of the state that this legislation could also mean that wildlife management districts that currently enjoy two weeks of muzzleloader season in central and southern regions of the state could be reduced to just one week. We acknowledge that some wildlife management districts on the edge of the northern districts and central/coastal districts may need some reevaluation and perhaps some may indeed qualify for an additional week. We would suggest that DIFW is in the best position to perform that evaluation, and would support them providing recommendations. To the extent that it is warranted, we would also urge the committee to provide the Department with the flexibility/authority they need to make these decisions in rule, rather than statute, if they feel they lack authority to do so. Thank you for your consideration, and we would be pleased to provide any information for the work session.
An organization of professional guides dedicated to promoting a quality, ethical outdoor experience.

TESTIMONY IN SUPPORT OF: LD 777 "An Act to Standardize the Muzzle-loading Season Statewide"
THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
SPONSORED BY: Representative Mason of Lisbon
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and fellow distinguished members of the inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Representative Rick Mason representing part
of Lisbon and l am here today to introduce my bill LD 777, "An Act to Standardize the Muzzle-
loading Season Statewide."
LD 777 establishes that the muzzle~loading-only open season on deer must be the same in all
areas of the State. Currently, differing regulations in the districts create an unfair situation for
those who live in those areas. These districts where originally closed due to snowfall pushing
deer into people's back yards where they would be easily harvested. The people in these districts should have the same hunting opportunities as others in our State. However, if snowfall is still a concern, the Commissioner should be allowed to open and close these districts
at their discretion.
I ask the committee to report this bill as "ought to pass" and I thank you for your time.

10036304:
3/10/2025
Esteemed Committee Members,
My name is Ron Greco and I run Moose Maine Kids. MMK is a 501c3 non-profit with a sole goal of increasing youth participation rates in traditional outdoor activities like hunting and fishing and providing kids with Critical Illnesses and Disabilities outdoor Dream Adventures. We are neither for nor against.
We applaud the potential for expanded opportunity to hunt. We also, in theory, support equal opportunities for all of Maine and Maine's people. However, we are deeply concerned about how this will technically be applied. There is good supportive biology for ending the season a week earlier in some zones in the north and west. Deer are in many cases on their way or inhabiting their traditional wintering areas. This puts hunting pressure on them when they are at their most vulnerable time. In the areas that allow a second week of muzzleloader hunting, the population supports this extra hunting pressure and the deer are mostly not congregating in wintering areas.
With these things in mind, I do not believe biology and good conservation science would support having the same muzzleloading season in all zones of the State. Fairness is not as equal. We have the same inequity in season for the moose hunt where the Southern zones of the state do not have the herd to support a moose hunting season. I encourage the committee to continue to support conservation science.
Thank you for your time!

185291:
TESTIMONY OF THE DEPARTMENT OF INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
BEFORE THE JOINT STANDING COMMITTEE ON INLAND FISHERIES AND WILDLIFE
IN OPPOSITION TO L.D. 777
"An Act to Standardize the Muzzle-loading Season Statewide"
Presented by: Representative MASON of Lisbon.
DATE OF HEARING: Monday, March 10, 2025
Good afternoon, Senator Baldacci, Representative Roberts and members of the Inland Fisheries and Wildlife Committee. I am Tim Peabody, Deputy Commissioner at the
Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife, speaking on behalf of the Department, in opposition to L.D. 777.
This bill establishes that the muzzleloading season for deer must be the same in all areas of the State. The current statute allows for greater flexibility setting different muzzleloader season lengths in different parts of the state, which has been used to set shorter seasons in the areas of the state that are more impacted by severe winter conditions.
Deer in northern and western Maine exist near the limits of their North American range and
are subject to severe winter conditions, which limit population growth potential. When winter
conditions arrive, particularly deep snow, deer follow historic migration routes to their
wintering areas, which may be natural deer wintering areas or in more recent times, around developed areas. When this snow arrives early, it is not uncommon for deer to be on these migration routes and headed to wintering areas while the hunting seasons are ongoing. As a
result, hunters in these areas of the state often express concerns that deer are being hunted on migration routes or in wintering areas, that it is unethical to hunt deer in these conditions, and
that an emergency season closure is needed. While in practice we have never closed the season early due to weather, we have seriously contemplated it and this bill would effectively
lengthen the hunting season in northern, western, and Downeast Maine and likely result in more public concern and requests for early season closures. While statute would still allow
the Commissioner to terminate the season in specific areas, when necessary, we do not
believe it would be good practice to rely on emergency season closures to routinely set appropriate seasons, and doing so would result in significant public frustration.
If the Committee is supportive, an alternative option to this bill could be for the Department to use its existing rulemaking authority to potentially add a second week of muzzleloader season in a limited number of additional Wildlife Management Districts where winter conditions are less severe. This could provide some additional hunting opportunities, while continuing to allow the Department flexibility to adjust season length and timing in response to deer population status, weather conditions, and social factors. I would be glad to answer any questions at this time or during the work session.
